name: Solutions k of max(m+d(m)) = k+2 for m<k; d(m) is the number of divisors of m.
comment: It is not known if there are other terms. There are no more terms < 10^10.
There are no more terms <= 10^12. - _Patrik Idén_, Jun 13 2026
There are no more terms <= 10^22. - _Daniel Veljjanoski_, Sep 13 2026
reference: R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, section B8.
link: Paul Erdős, Some Unconventional Problems in Number Theory, Math. Mag. 52(2) (Mar. 1979), 67-70. See p. 68 (Problem 4).
Patrik Idén, Computational Verification of Erdős Problem 647 up to 10^12: Gap-Growth Analysis, Depth-Record Extension to D=11, and Structural Analysis, Zenodo preprint v3, 2026.
Ibrahim Mian and Shayaan Siddique, A Kernel-Checked Exclusion Certificate for Erdős Problem 647, arXiv:2608.17880 [cs.LO], 2026. See pp. 1, 3, 6.
Daniel Veljjanoski, Erdős problem 647: exhaustive search, no further terms up to 10^22, GitHub, 2026.
example: The largest value of m+d(m) for m < n=8 is 6+d(6)=10 = n+2, so 8 is in the sequence.
program: (PARI) isok(k) = if (k>1, vecmax(vector(k-1, m, m+numdiv(m))) == k+2); \\ _Michel Marcus_, Aug 21 2026
author: _Jud McCranie_, Aug 28 2003
